title: Winnipeg police officers cleared in fatal shooting
article: A police watch dog has cleared two Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) officers after a police chase in 2017 ended with a suspect fatally shot.

The Independent Investigation Unit (IIU) said on September 13, 2017 shortly after midnight a 23-year-old Winnipeg man suspected of robbery, assault, and carjacking that same evening was driving a stolen vehicle in the area of Powers Steer and Alfred Avenue. Followed by the WPS Helicopter AIR1, the man stopped the vehicle and exited carrying a gun. IIU said when officers moved in the man pointed the gun at his head. Officers ordered the man to put down the weapon multiple times at which point the man pointed the gun at officers. Two members of the WPS Tactical Support Team then shot the man. He was taken to the Health Sciences Centre where he was pronounced dead. It was later determined the man had been carrying a replica gun.

Following an extensive investigation by the IIU which included nearly 40 interviews of civilian and officer witnesses, reviews of police radio transmissions and various videos of the incident, it was determined that the actions of two WPS officers was "justifiable and unavoidable."

"[The suspect's] action of pointing his weapon at a police officer is consistent with a person who wishes to instigate a police shooting to accomplish that purpose," IIU Civilian Director Zane Tessler wrote in a report of the investigation. "This is an unfortunate yet all too familiar circumstance seen across Canada and the United States in situations similar to this."
The IIU said it has concluded the investigation into the incident and an inquest into the death will take place as required under the Fatality Inquiries Act.
